The House GOP's proposed Medicaid cuts would devastate Georgia families by slashing federal support for ACA subsidies and gutting coverage protections. Their plan converts Medicaid into per-capita caps—a bureaucratic trick designed to underfund states by $900B over a decade while shifting costs onto taxpayers. 

By axing enhanced ACA expansion funds (which cover 90% of costs), Georgia would face a 57% premium spike for 109k residents in GA-04—forcing low-income families to pay $15k+ extra annually. This isn’t fiscal responsibility—it’s a deliberate sabotage of healthcare access to fund tax breaks for corporate donors. 

D.C.’s math is simple: protect Pharma profits, torch working-class coverage.

The Save America’s Rural Hospitals Act (H.R. 3684) throws $55 million at bureaucratic band-aids while failing to address systemic bloat. Rural hospitals are collapsing not from lack of funding but from decades of mismanagement and Medicaid fraud. The real issue? Washington funnels cash into administrative overhead and redundant programs instead of patient care.

For every dollar spent on rural healthcare, 30 cents vanish into compliance paperwork and middlemen. The GOP’s focus should be slashing red tape, not expanding a broken system.

Meanwhile, the Affordable Care Act’s expiring subsidies reveal a deeper rot: 40% of Georgia’s Medicaid budget leaks into waste, yet Congress keeps writing blank checks. Fix the pipes before flooding the basement.

See how the numbers expose the real drivers of rural hospital decline: https://t.co/q0DLvPeqvq

The Big Beautiful Bill’s fatal flaw? It targets coverage for working Americans while leaving pharma middlemen and bloated Medicaid consultants untouched. Section 3(b) alone carves out $200B in loopholes for hospital billing firms—proving D.C. cares more about padding corporate margins than streamlining care.

Georgia’s 93K Medicaid cuts? A direct result of prioritizing paperwork over patients. Real reform would slash administrative bloat, not lifelines.

Audit the waste, protect the vulnerable, and watch how fast $1.6T in cuts materializes without stripping coverage. Until then, this bill’s just another D.C. shell game—robbing Main Street to fund K Street.

The real issue isn’t expiring subsidies—it’s the ACA’s structural failure to address systemic waste and corporate profiteering. For years, Washington funneled billions into bloated subsidies while ignoring the root causes: hospital price-gouging, Big Pharma’s monopoly pricing, and Medicaid fraud. The ACA’s temporary fixes didn’t lower costs; they masked them with taxpayer-funded Band-Aids.

Now, bureaucrats panic when the money runs dry. Instead of demanding endless subsidies, let’s overhaul a broken system. Cut the middlemen, expose medical billing scams, and force providers to compete.

Real reform means market-driven affordability, not perpetual dependence on D.C. slush funds.
